list.name: difficulty
list.label: Difficulty
list.description: Filters the panels whose metrics carry a difficulty label.

panels.title: Divers online now
panels.description: Distinct seated connections right now (scraped every 15s).

panels.title: Rooms live
panels.description: Rooms with at least one seated diver connected — a lobby counts, a crusade mid-mission counts, a resumed session counts.

panels.title: Crusades launched · range
panels.description: START_DIVE actions: a crusade launched from a room lobby. Not counted: rooms created, sessions resumed from a save, or solo play run locally in the browser.

panels.title: Missions started · range
panels.description: Every mission that began: the crusade's first dive plus each ADVANCE. This is the gameplay-volume number the old "Dives started" panel was missing.

panels.title: Mission success · range
panels.description: Success share of honor-system mission reports. Directional, not ground truth.

panels.title: Saved dives · cap 500
panels.description: Rooms pinned so they outlive the idle TTL. Nearing 500 means the save cap starts evicting the oldest pinned crusades.

panels.title: Cold HTTP hits by route
panels.description: Server-reached requests only: client-side navigation and the PWA service worker are invisible, so read it as arrivals, not page views.

panels.title: Rooms created — fresh vs resumed
panels.description: A fresh room is a new lobby. A resumed room seeds a live crusade from a personal session save — the return path that never fires START_DIVE.

panels.title: Join attempts by result
panels.description: Every WebSocket hello. room_not_found is a dead or expired invite link; locked means the share link was opened while the squad was in rewards/forfeit; bad_code and rate_limited are protocol noise or probes.

panels.title: Room lookups — invite-link health
panels.description: GET /api/rooms/:code, driven by the Bridge's resume list and pre-join checks. A rising missing share is dead links.

panels.title: Refused room creations
panels.description: cap = the 2000-room ceiling (the single machine is full); rate_limited = an address making more than 10 rooms a minute; invalid_save = a malformed session file.

panels.title: HTTP errors by route
panels.description: 4xx/5xx cold hits. Repeated api_room misses are dead links; 5xx is worth a look at fly logs.

panels.title: Presence
panels.description: Seated divers and rooms with a live connection. Presence says who is connected, never whether a mission is running — pair it with the funnel.

panels.title: Rooms by phase
panels.description: Every stored room's phase, refreshed by the 2-minute census. A fat lobby band is unlaunched rooms; a standing forfeit band is a stuck squad.

panels.title: Rooms by difficulty
panels.description: Where the ladder currently sits: the census gauge keyed by each room's difficulty.

panels.title: Missions started, reported per hour
panels.description: The honest volume line: missions opened per hour, split into reported successes and failures.

panels.title: Volume funnel
panels.description: Volumes, not conversion: rooms created → arrivals seated → missions started → missions reported → operations completed → crusades achieved. Each bar counts a different population (arrivals can exceed rooms when people rejoin), so read it as how deep play gets.

panels.title: Time in phase — p95
panels.description: How long rooms spend in a phase before moving on. Lobby p95 is onboarding friction; pacts/decision p95 is how long the host's buttons wait.

panels.title: Risk & balance — is chosen risk real?
Valor at report
panels.description: The risk each diver actually staked when the mission reported, read from the engine's own selector. If this sits near zero, missions run at the base tier and the reward ladder is decoration.

panels.title: Zero-Valor reports
panels.description: Share of reports taken with nothing at stake — declined directive, no pacts, no strain. The design wants this to be a choice, not the default.

panels.title: Rolled ceilings · range
panels.description: The tier each report actually rolled. The risk economy realized — and the only place S/S+ shows up in the wild.

panels.title: Pacts sworn per diver · range
panels.description: How many pacts each present diver locked per mission, in exact counts derived from the histogram buckets.

panels.title: Squad directive calls
panels.description: Accepted vs declined. Flips in the pact window count again — the label says which way a call was made, not the squad's final word.

panels.title: Directive accept rate by difficulty
panels.description: Are squads braver as the ladder climbs? A flat low rate everywhere means the carrot is not landing.

panels.title: Directive accept rate by rule — top 12
panels.description: Rules squads say yes to. A rule at ~0% is dead weight; a rule at ~100% is free Valor.

panels.title: Pacts sworn by rule — top 12
panels.description: Which pacts divers actually take. Never-taken pacts are content not paying rent; auto-taken ones may be too cheap.

panels.title: Rule trouble — failed pacts, failed directives, refused accepts
panels.description: The three ways a rule misfires: broken in the field (too hard or unclear), or refused at the wheel because it would strand a diver below four stratagems (unfieldable). Top 8 each.

panels.title: Strain calls
panels.description: The operation-long subfaction commitment: accepted or declined, per strain.

panels.title: Major Order mix · range
panels.description: live = playing toward the actual war order (pays the token carrot); manual = a front picked by hand; cleared = order removed before the draw.

panels.title: Win rate by difficulty
panels.description: Success share per difficulty. Where the curve collapses, the ladder stops being fun — watch restarts next to this.

panels.title: Average stars by difficulty
panels.description: Stars drive reward options (and the honors cadence), so this is the performance curve behind the loot economy. Failures are excluded — they award none.

panels.title: Reported time remaining
panels.description: The extraction clock people type in. Rushing (low) versus full-clearing (high) — and the input to the sample-haul multiplier.

panels.title: Sample hauls by rarity
panels.description: Average samples reported per successful mission, next to what the maps hold (SAMPLE_AVAILABILITY). Big gaps mean squads report less than they extract.

panels.title: Rewards picked by tier · range
panels.description: What the draft actually banks. Watch for C-tier picks at difficulty 6+ — that is the early-game loot curve leaking upward.

panels.title: Requisition purchases by tier · range
panels.description: Whether Brasch's Bargains is affordable: a shelf nobody buys is a shelf priced wrong.

panels.title: Forfeits by tier · range
panels.description: What failure actually costs: the tier of the items divers gave up after a failed mission.

panels.title: Honors spun / awarded · range
panels.description: The end-of-mission ceremony. Awards lag spins when the host skips naming a winner — the ceremony is a soft gate by design.

panels.title: Reward tokens spent · range
panels.description: Rerolls vs bans. Tokens are the honors carrot — if they never get spent, the carrot is invisible.

panels.title: Wheel rerolls by wheel · range
panels.description: Where the reroll economy goes: misfortune, front or strain. Front rerolls are the operation's one narrow window.

panels.title: Returning divers by silence gap · range
panels.description: A known seat (or a reclaimed cache) coming back after the room went quiet. Without accounts this is the best retention signal there is: <1h is the same evening, >1d is the next session.

panels.title: Seats taken, by kind
panels.description: New divers, mid-crusade joiners (Field Promotion) and reclaimed caches — how squads actually fill up.

panels.title: Seats left & host transfers
panels.description: Departures by kind plus host migrations. Frequent disconnects-era transfers mean the host role, not the squad, is the fragile part.

panels.title: Squad size at mission start · range
panels.description: Present divers when a mission opened, in exact counts. The design's squad-size rules should be tuned to whatever this bar chart says.

panels.title: Stepping away vs coming back
panels.description: The 30-second grace window in action: divers who dropped mid-crusade and divers whose seats woke back up.

panels.title: Rooms swept by TTL · range
panels.description: Idle rooms the sweeper reaped because nobody saved them. A high number with recent activity means the TTLs are too short for real play rhythms.

panels.title: Warbond edits · range
panels.description: Explicit warbond declarations. The default is everyone-owns-everything, so only edits carry signal about real purchases.

panels.title: Process CPU
panels.description: The single shared-cpu-1x machine. Presence spikes cost very little — watch this only when other numbers move with it.

panels.title: Memory RSS
panels.description: 256 MB is the machine's ceiling. Rooms are fully in memory while live, so this one is worth an eye at growth.

panels.title: Event loop lag p99
panels.description: The room server's responsiveness ceiling — a sync core that blocks shows up here before players feel it.

panels.title: Running build
panels.description: The image and engine version serving right now. The restart annotation on every panel comes from the same signal.
